caption_or_description: (a) Nellie Newton presses against the surface, mg (action), and the surface presses on Nellie, N (reaction). So mg and N are equal and opposite. (b) Nellie presses with less force against the inclined surface, so in action–reaction fashion, the normal force N is correspondingly smaller. (c) The component of mg perpendicular to the sloped surface has the same magnitude as N; the component of mg parallel to the surface provides acceleration.
As the incline steepens, the normal force N on a block of ice diminishes, and N is zero when the incline is vertical.
(a) On friction-free ice, only mg and N act on the shoe. (b) On the wooden board, a force of friction f is present. (c) At equilibrium, the resultant of N and mg is equal and opposite to f.
